jurisdiction.name: Morocco
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Morocco has no AI-specific law; AI governance runs through the digital strategy, data-protection regulation and a recent layer of election and sector rules. The Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform leads policy through the Digital Morocco 2030 strategy (2024), which names AI as an accelerator, and the first National AI Conference (July 2025), whose synthesis report calls for an AI legal framework, an ethics regulator and a national ethics charter. Binding obligations come mainly from Law 09-08 on personal data, enforced by the CNDP, which imposed a facial-recognition moratorium in 2019 and since 2020 allows the technology only with prior authorisation; the CNDP opened hearings on AI in March 2025 with a view to a dedicated deliberation. For the September 2026 elections, Organic Law 53.25 explicitly covers offences committed with AI tools, the audiovisual regulator HACA banned misleading AI-generated electoral content on radio and TV, and the CNDP required AI content to be flagged. Constitutional advisory councils (CESE in 2024, CSEFRS in 2026 for education) have called for a national AI strategy and framework; a digital-administration bill with AI provisions and an AI roadmap ('Maroc IA 2030') are announced but not yet published.

Haute Autorité de la Communication Audiovisuelle (HACA)

narrative.review_notes: Deep review 2026-10-06 (resumed from an interrupted run; earlier downloads re-checked by hash against the live official URLs). No instruments existed before; 11 added, all read from official PDFs except Decree 2-09-165 (scanned image). Arabic BO text of Organic Law 53.25 has a poorly encoded header; the BO date (29 January 2026) is read from it. Sites that blocked automated reading: chambredesrepresentants.ma (Cloudflare challenge), so private members' AI bills could not be read; dgssi.gov.ma French pages reset the connection. The CSEFRS French PDF URL returns 404; the Arabic PDF was used. Considered and not recorded: DGSSI National Cybersecurity Strategy 2030 (mentions AI only as an emerging-technology training need, no AI guidance); Law 05-20 on cybersecurity (no AI provisions); CNDP press release of 18 March 2025 on AI and personal data (press release announcing hearings, no guidance document); HACA study on AI in audiovisual production (study, not an instrument); Penal Code Article 447-2 (deepfake-type offence but no explicit AI wording, not verified on an official full-text source). Morocco is listed in AU and UNESCO regional files (Continental AI Strategy, UNESCO Recommendation apply automatically); it is not listed as a party/signatory in data/regional/COE.json for CETS 225 and no official Moroccan signature was found. Convention 108 accession (2019) is recited in CNDP deliberations but is a data-protection treaty, not recorded here. News sites were used only for discovery.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 09-08 relative à la protection des personnes physiques à l'égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 09-08 on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data (promulgated by Dahir No. 1-09-15 of 18 February 2009)
instruments.issuing_authority: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.publisher_name: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.current_status: In force; published in Bulletin Officiel No. 5714 of 5 March 2009. Text read from the CNDP copy of the BO French edition.
instruments.summary: Morocco's general data protection law, which governs any processing of personal data, including AI training and deployment that uses such data, and creates the CNDP as supervisory authority. It sets lawfulness, purpose, proportionality and transparency rules, prior declaration or authorisation of processing, data-subject rights and cross-border transfer limits; Article 11 bars court decisions assessing a person's behaviour from being based on automated processing intended to evaluate aspects of their personality.
metadata_gaps: Entry-into-force date not stated in the text (published in BO No. 5714 of 5 March 2009; transitional regime in Article 67)
French text is the BO French edition; the Arabic text is the authoritative version

instruments.summary: Implementing decree for Law 09-08 that organises the CNDP and the procedures for declarations, authorisations and transfers of personal data. instruments.official_title: Délibération n° D-194-2019 du 30/08/2019 relative à un moratoire sur la reconnaissance faciale
instruments.english_title: CNDP Deliberation No. D-194-2019 of 30 August 2019 on a moratorium on facial recognition
instruments.issuing_authority: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.publisher_name: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.current_status: Expired 31 March 2020, extended by Deliberation D-97-2020 to 31 December 2020 (as recited in D-195-EUS/2020); replaced by the facial-recognition usage framework in D-195-EUS/2020.
instruments.summary: The CNDP imposed a seven-month moratorium, from 2 September 2019, on the use of facial recognition, during which it would issue no authorisations for the technique. The pause was meant to allow a broad consultation of public, private, civil-society and expert stakeholders before a deliberation framing the purposes for which facial recognition may be used.

instruments.official_title: Délibération n° D-195-EUS/2020 du 30/12/2020 relative à la définition de l'usage des technologies de reconnaissance faciale
instruments.english_title: CNDP Deliberation No. D-195-EUS/2020 of 30 December 2020 defining the use of facial recognition technologies
instruments.issuing_authority: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.publisher_name: Commission Nationale de contrôle de la protection des Données à caractère Personnel (CNDP)
instruments.current_status: Adopted 30 December 2020 in the context of the health state of emergency; recalls sector deliberations D-108-EUS/2020 (remote bank accounts) and D-126-EUS/2020 (social-security proof of life).
instruments.summary: Ends the facial-recognition moratorium by allowing data controllers to use facial recognition after prior authorisation from the CNDP, provided they commit to switch authentication to the national trusted third-party identity system once it is available and design their systems to allow that switch. The CNDP states strong reservations about each provider building its own biometric base (sometimes hosted abroad) and recommends separating usage and authentication data.

instruments.current_status: Published by the CNDP on 3 August 2026 ahead of the 23 September 2026 legislative elections.
instruments.summary: One-page CNDP guidance for parties, candidates and other actors processing personal data in the 2026 elections. Among ten rules grounded in Law 09-08, it requires flagging any AI-produced content, citing Article 447-2 of the Penal Code and Articles 39, 51 and 53 of Organic Law 53-25 on the House of Representatives.

instruments.current_status: Promulgated by Dahir No. 1.25.70 of 16 January 2026 after Constitutional Court decision No. 259/25 of 24 December 2025; published in Bulletin Officiel (Arabic edition) No. 7478. Not AI-specific: a general electoral law with explicit AI provisions.
instruments.summary: Amends the organic law on elections to the House of Representatives and adds explicit references to 'artificial intelligence tools' in the electoral offences. It criminalises spreading false news, defamatory or fabricated content, unlawful use of a person's voice or image, and making content with false or falsified material intended to undermine the integrity of elections, when done by any means including AI tools, social networks or online platforms, with prison terms and fines (amended Articles 39, 51 and 53 and following).
metadata_gaps: BO issue date read from a poorly encoded header (BO No. 7478, 9 Chaabane 1447 = 29 January 2026)
Effective date: Article 3 applies the law to the next House of Representatives elections held after its publication

instruments.current_status: Adopted 16 June 2026; applies during the electoral period 15 August–22 September 2026. Article 30 provides for publication in the Bulletin Officiel (BO reference not checked).
instruments.summary: Binding rules for public and private radio and TV services during the 2026 electoral period (15 August to 22 September 2026). Article 6 bars broadcasters from airing electoral content generated or altered by AI that could mislead the public or harm the integrity of the debate; such content may be aired only for information, explanation or verification, with a clear, permanent label, and must not simulate a real person's appearance, voice or identity unless this is visibly disclosed.

instruments.current_status: Presented September 2024; ministry page dated 25 September 2024 hosts the institutional brochure (FR/EN). AI-specific roadmap 'Maroc IA 2030' announced in 2026 has no published document yet (see leads).
instruments.summary: Morocco's national digital strategy to 2030, aiming to make the country a digital hub. It rests on two axes, digitising public services for citizens and businesses and boosting the digital economy, with artificial intelligence, cloud and digital talent named as accelerators; headline targets include 240,000 digital jobs and a MAD 100 billion contribution to GDP by 2030.
metadata_gaps: Official document is an image-only institutional brochure (French and English versions); content read from page images, no text layer

instruments.current_status: Published 29 September 2025 in Arabic, Amazigh, French and English. A conference report, not an adopted strategy.
instruments.summary: Official synthesis of the first national AI conference held in Rabat on 1–2 July 2025, setting out orientations for a sovereign, ethical and inclusive national AI roadmap under Digital Morocco 2030. It records calls for an AI legal framework (the minister announced a bill in preparation), an ethics regulator, a national AI ethics charter, sovereign infrastructure, skills and sector adoption.

instruments.english_title: CESE Opinion: What uses and prospects for the development of artificial intelligence in Morocco? (Own-initiative opinion No. 78/2024)
instruments.current_status: Adopted unanimously by the CESE General Assembly at its 159th ordinary session on 27 June 2024; PDF posted November 2024. Advisory, not binding.
instruments.summary: Own-initiative opinion of the constitutional Economic, Social and Environmental Council on AI uses and prospects in Morocco. It finds no specific regulatory framework, slow open-data release, skills gaps and fragmented R&D, and calls for a national AI strategy aligned with the country's ambitions, together with recommendations on governance, ethics, data, skills and financing.

instruments.summary: Recommendation of the constitutional Higher Council for Education, Training and Scientific Research noting that generative AI has entered schools faster than institutional rules. It calls for a national guidance framework for AI in education, training and research, setting institutional and regulatory foundations, guiding principles (including the child's best interests), alignment of short-term measures with strategy, family awareness and learner participation.

leads.note: CNDP launched hearings on 18 March 2025 (https://www.cndp.ma/ia-pdp/) to prepare a deliberation on AI; hearings ran into 2025. No deliberation published by 2026-10-06.

leads.title: مشروع قانون الإدارة الرقمية
leads.english_title: Draft Digital Administration Law (with AI provisions)
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform (MTNRA)
leads.note: Ministry stated in a written answer to the House of Representatives (14 July 2025) that it prepared a digital-administration bill including AI-specific provisions. No official draft found on sgg.gov.ma or parliament sites.

leads.title: مقترح قانون يتعلق بتنظيم استعمال الذكاء الاصطناعي
leads.english_title: Private members' bill on regulating the use of artificial intelligence (House of Representatives)
leads.issuing_authority: House of Representatives (Mouvement Populaire parliamentary group)
leads.note: 17-article bill reported by press; chambredesrepresentants.ma blocks automated reading (Cloudflare), so the official text, number and date were not verified.

leads.title: Feuille de route « Maroc IA 2030 » / « AI Made in Morocco »
leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform (MTNRA)
leads.note: Roadmap launched 12 January 2026 (MEN news page) with an implementation update on 8 September 2026; no official roadmap document found online.

leads.title: Stratégie IA de l'AMMC
leads.english_title: AMMC artificial intelligence strategy and roadmap
leads.issuing_authority: Autorité Marocaine du Marché des Capitaux (AMMC)
leads.note: AMMC 2026 priorities mention progressive AI integration and an AI strategy; no standalone AI document published.
